result.title: WildAIGC-Bench: Can AI Image Detectors Handle the Wild? A Benchmark of Generated and Edited Images in Online Circulation
result.summary: AI-generated images linked to news events and online claims can mislead audiences, enable fraud, or cause public controversy. We introduce WildAIGC-Bench, built through recurring collection across news websites, fact-checking sources, and related social media content. The pipeline combines broad coverage, timely updates, and human-verified labels through scheduled discovery, automatic screening and preliminary annotation, and human review of image-specific evidence. The benchmark contains 407 verified AI-generated or edited images, each accompanied by a source webpage link and an evidence summary. Images retain the conditions encountered online, including compression, screenshots, and recapture. Evaluation of dedicated visual detectors, multimodal large language models, and a simple Perception Encoder baseline reveals substantial recall gaps relative to existing benchmarks. WildAIGC-Bench provides both a practical detection challenge and a basis for continued data expansion and source-based verification. The dataset is released at https://github.com/YuZijian/WildAIGC-Bench.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文构建了来自真实网络传播场景的 AI 生成/编辑图像检测基准，包含 407 张经人工核验的图片及来源网页与证据摘要，并在压缩、截图、翻拍等条件下评测专用检测器、多模态大模型和编码器基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于生成图像取证与检测基准，聚焦检测器召回率而非模型内部视觉状态、latent 推理轨迹或证据获取与停止决策，与 LVR 主线缺少实质联系，也无具体可迁移的方法线索。
